shape.name: Shape C — Test-Teach-Test
shape.description: Students are tested on error recognition first, teacher clarifies rules for problematic items, then freer production follows.
shape.pedagogical_justification: Students already have implicit knowledge of capitalisation and punctuation rules from prior exposure. The diagnostic test (Task 1) reveals which specific rules they struggle with. The teacher then clarifies only the problematic patterns (Task 2), followed by a freer writing task (Task 3) where students apply the rules in a paragraph.
shape.main_aim_format: By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to identify and correct common punctuation and capitalisation errors in their own writing.

example_lesson_plan.header:
Objective:
By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to identify and correct common punctuation and capitalisation errors in their own writing.
Teacher:
Ed Rush
Date:
21 July, 2026
Duration:
46 minutes
CEFR Level:
B2
Lesson Shape:
C (Test-Teach-Test)
Materials:
Punctuation & Capitalisation Workshop worksheet, slideshow
Assessment:
Error correction answer key (Task 1), rule explanations (Task 2), written paragraph (Task 3)
Systems:
Punctuation, Capitalisation

stages.stage_aim: To activate students' awareness of their own writing errors and frame the lesson value.
procedure: Display the title slide: 'How can I make my writing less messy?' — elicit responses from students.
Show the 'Why is this lesson important?' slide. Read the bullet points aloud. Ask: 'Do you make these mistakes in your writing?'
State the objective: today we will fix punctuation and capitalisation errors.

stages.stage_aim: To focus students on the target language (capitalisation of 'I') through a concrete example.
procedure: Show the Example slide (auto-animate: i → I).
Ask: 'What is wrong here?' Elicit that 'i' should be capitalised.
Press right arrow to show the corrected version with yellow highlight on 'I'.
CCQ: 'Why is i wrong? What should it be?' (Answer: The pronoun I is always capitalised.)

stages.stage_aim: To diagnostically assess which punctuation and capitalisation errors students can identify independently.
procedure: Show the 'Task 1 — Recognise' transition slide (red).
Review instructions: Circle each error, write the correction above.
Point out that Question 1 has 2 errors — demonstrate the process.
Start the 8-minute timer. Students work individually on the worksheet, finding errors in all 10 sentences.
After the timer ends, go through each sentence one at a time using the auto-animate answer slides. For each: show the error, then click to reveal the corrected version with yellow highlighting.
Students mark their own work in a different colour.

stages.stage_aim: To clarify the rules behind the most common error patterns so students understand why each correction is needed.
procedure: Show the 'Task 2 — Recall' slide (red). Review instructions: explain each rule in one complete sentence.
Start the 5-minute timer. Students write rule explanations for the 4 items (Manager, comma spacing, The, however).
After the timer, review each rule slide. For each: read the rule, ask CCQs to check understanding.

Key rules to cover: (1) The pronoun I is always capitalised, (2) Common nouns are not capitalised, (3) No space before a comma, (4) Use comma after introductory phrases, (5) Use commas around extra information, (6) Use semicolon before 'however'.

stages.stage_aim: To give students freer written practice applying all punctuation and capitalisation rules in their own writing.
procedure: Show the 'Task 3 — Use' slide (red). Explain the task: write a ~70-word paragraph about a difficult decision.
Review the checklist items: subordinate conjunction, appositive in commas, comma before and/but, correct use of 'however'.
Start the 8-minute timer. Students write individually. Circulate and provide support.
Collect paragraphs for assessment. Focus feedback on punctuation and capitalisation.

metadata.main_aim: By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to identify and correct common punctuation and capitalisation errors in their own writing.
metadata.subsidiary_aim: Students will review the rules for capitalisation of proper nouns, comma usage (introductory phrases, appositives, compound sentences), and semicolon use with 'however'.
answer_key: Q5: Add commas around 'who is 68 years old' + Teacher→teacher
Q6: Add comma after 'In my opinion' + lowercase 't'
Q9: Add semicolon before 'however' + comma after
R1: Common nouns (manager) are not capitalised — only proper nouns.
R2: No space before a comma; space after.
R3: After an introductory clause, comma + lowercase letter.
